judge: Claude (Opus 5.5), acting as answer key for the owner
method: Viewed each site's desktop top (1440x900), projects section screenshot and phone top (390x844), captured locally on 2026-11-13, plus the first ~1,500 characters of the page text, in a shuffled order that hid stored scores. Scored each 0-100 from a recruiter's and peer's eye (design craft, clarity in 5 seconds, project substance, writing, memorability), then sorted and broke ties by hand. No Gemini output was seen before this file was written.

ranking.reason: Custard: refined serif editorial design, a specific research focus, reproducible case studies with real numbers, excellent writing; pseudonym instead of a name.
Dhruv Parmar: technical-drawing concept carried through, strong type, case studies with real scope; mobile hero cut off.
Jos (jos.gg): pixel-art identity, live player count, testimonials, founder of a game studio; distinctive and specific.
Ameer Muavia Shah: projects page, elegant serif editorial with a warm palette, own ventures plus many real client systems, clear writing ("Work built for real life").

Devesh Chandan: polished light editorial hero with big type around a portrait, specific about text and strong projects (code-hosting platform with CLI, a placed hackathon fintech build); role reads "Backend" on desktop and "Full stack" on phones.
Masab Qurban: bold editorial hero (name behind a portrait), warm neutral palette, specific project blurbs (79 calculators, a solar company's invoicing); stat fluff.
Vishvajeet Shukla: polished freelance-studio site, serif display, confident writing ("Design that ships"); only 2 client products shown.
Anthony Mahefa: striking 3D sphere and bold outlined type, clear role, three real client products with case studies; a sound pop-up covers content, text runs over the graphic.
Ashutosh Dash: playful neo-brutalist look with a memory game in the hero, clear role, experience bullets with measured results; analytics banner covers content, small side projects.
Hussam Barqawi: polished dark AI-builder site with a clear focus and project cards that describe real systems; filler stats, "I'm an" typewriter shows blank.
Ali Linares: clean Swiss-style layout with sidebars, good hierarchy; generic headline, "projects" are jobs with concrete outcomes.

Abdul Rehman Waseem: crisp minimal profile-card layout with nice touches (pull cord, pronunciation); a leaked CSS class name shows as text, role differs between views; founder of a live product, 14 projects, hackathon wins.
Mahmoud Zalt: polished AI-consultancy site with a live product and a clear offer; salesy, stat fluff ("101+ projects"), endless tech marquee.
Andre Nunes da Silva: compact, tidy student site; standout projects (own Scheme-like language in C, a coding agent); small type, little visual identity.
Samarth Batra: Windows-desktop metaphor, memorable and well executed; strong experience (Amazon, Leidos); overlapping windows cluttered, projects behind a click.
Kieran (althruist): playful hand-drawn type over game art, a clear game-dev identity and a personal voice; projects shown only as thumbnails, logo pill overlaps the heading on phones.
Farhan Segujja: warm patterned light theme and an illustrated portrait; honest, specific writing about scope; the phone view is visibly broken (clipped circle).
Ajyendu Chaudhary: 3D keycaps and big display type, a playful cat; the name runs into the keyboard and off the phone screen; a real internship with measured results.
Aggelos Ladas: clean dark layout with a fake API console that suits a backend role but sits empty; solid student projects (Spring e-shop, Android app, a haptic wearable for deaf athletes).
Rajwardhan Patil: the listed URL is a projects page, so no name or role up top; strong editorial layout and ambitious projects (live code editor, urban-heat AI).
Vineet Machchal: clean light modern layout, self-taught; small but real projects (bakery site, client portfolio, Discord bot); generic code-card hero.
Sambhu S Babu: clear niche (Frappe/ERPNext freelancer in Kerala) and tidy dark layout; SEO-style headline, projects live on another page.
Ashleigh Simonelli: retro CRT with a Rick and Morty terminal intro and a Blockbuster nostalgia wall; unforgettable, but the intro hides who she is and what she does.
Oussama Sallak: purple-neon template with "Welcome to my portfolio" and a cut typewriter line; real substance below (MLOps platform, 45% inference cost cut).
Pavan Gupta: dark neon dev template with terminal gimmick; clear name and role; real projects with demos but filler stats ("50+ projects") and typos.
Loren Kamau: restrained one-column serif layout, calm and readable; corporate-generic copy and only two thin project blurbs.
Hafid Ziti: dated sky-blue hero with a stock illustration; clear senior role, jobs at IBM and Eaton shown as project cards buried in logo tag walls.
Mohammad Huzaifa: generic light template, the role changes between views (Full-Stack, AI & DS, Angular & .NET), "100% commitment" fluff; student projects are varied and real.
Anton Manaev: blurred gradient with low-contrast subtitle, "Initiate system", buzzword copy and fluff stats; real client work (Shopify store, Upwork extension) in a carousel.
Abhishek Kumar T: student, busy terminal theme; one solid ML project with a measured result, two small landing pages.
Mario Kandut: consultancy page with a cookie banner over content, a typewriter headline cut mid-word, stack lists and 2023 blog posts; no projects on the page.
Abhijeet Bhale: wave-graphic hero with an outlined name; mobile hero is broken (name overflows, nothing else); projects with screenshots and demos, inflated copy.
Pawaret Muengkaew: "Hi there!" with no role on desktop, a skill-icon wall, "passionate developer"; real work history but no projects visible.
Arka Mahajan: 3D board hero with the name and role printed over it (hard to read), the phone view stuck on a boot loader, broken "0+ projects / 0 CGPA" counters, thin projects.
Nikhil Kumawat: neon network-particle template, student projects (food delivery app, stats card), a typo in a project title ("Dekstop").
Asfakur Nariz: dark template, role flips between UI/UX designer and full stack, the same job blurb pasted under three jobs, "passionate", "pixel-perfect".
Aditya Kumar: stock centered-caps template, cliché copy ("with finesse"), blog and social-network clone projects.
Nguyen Van Qui: a resume pasted as a page, dense monospace bullets, generic About; work is real but nothing is presented as projects.
Toukoum: an AI-chat template ("Build your AI portfolio" link) showing "Hey, I'm Aaaaby"; nothing to read without chatting, no visible work.
Sameer: one red screen with a name, a Capricorn glyph and "A passionate front-end developer"; nothing else on the page, awkward "Hello There!, I'm-".
